markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

Starting-point insights: (1) The reported recent-residual/CE score, 0.5238 versus SASRec’s 0.5050, motivates replication; it does not isolate either component’s contribution. (2) User feedback identifies stale isolated evidence and broad resemblance without a current connection. Recent, repeated context could address both, but cannot establish compatibility. (3) Electronics has 20.2% sampled training reversals and a −0.7499 tenth-percentile margin. This supports testing discrimination objectives, without establishing a generalization bottleneck.

Related-work insights: (1) SASRec [1] supplies a global sequential representation. Retaining it protects potentially useful older interests. (2) ScaleRec [2] motivates multiple context lengths rather than assuming five interactions always define an intent. Fixed windows provide a cheaper initial comparison than learned segmentation. (3) Objective comparisons [3] distinguish sampled candidate discrimination from full-catalog optimization. Multi-negative CE therefore remains a hypothesis requiring controlled validation.

### Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed test | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context | SASRec; five-item residual | Gated 1/5/20-item pools | Which history scale helps? |
| Discrimination | Single-negative BCE | Uniform 64-negative CE | Training separation versus validation ranking |
| Specificity | ID associations | From-scratch title fusion | Text resemblance versus actual usefulness |

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each score includes a positive and negative assessment.

| Idea | Assessments: score (+strength; −limitation) |
|---|---|
| **A. Multi-scale residual + CE** [1–3] | O 3 (+controlled combination; −established components); P 7 (+adaptive context; −incremental); U 8 (+stale and broad-interest failures; −no compatibility evidence); M 8 (+negative competition; −in-sample rationale); D 4 (+small modules; −sampler/predictor coordination) |
| B. Five-item residual + gBCE [1,4] | O 2 (+clear comparator; −standard components); P 6 (+objective evidence; −transfer uncertain); U 6 (+current context and specificity; −fixed scope); M 8 (+discrimination test; −calibration unproven); D 4 (+simple loss; −exact weighting essential) |
| C. Gated title/description fusion + recent pooling [1] | O 4 (+permitted content; −known fusion); P 7 (+sparse-item support; −weak text supervision); U 7 (+specific identification and recency; −lexical shortcuts); M 5 (+shared item evidence; −indirect margin mechanism); D 6 (+trainable locally; −tokenization and inference cost) |

### Selected experiment

At 10% progress, select A. Preserve SASRec normalization; add a small scalar-gated projection of causally pooled raw item embeddings over windows 1, 5 and 20. Repeated occurrences contribute repeated evidence. This targets stale isolated influence and broad-interest recommendations lacking current support; CE targets Electronics’ measured separation weakness. These are mechanisms, not demonstrated improvements.

Compare baseline, CE-only, multi-scale-only and combined, retaining baseline eligibility. Select completed configurations using pinned macro validation HR@10 within the remaining shared budget. Track category results, sampled reversals, gate weights and residual norms. History sensitivity remains unmeasured; embedding alignment does not establish collapse.

idea.description: Test a lightweight multi-scale recent-interest residual with uniform multi-negative candidate cross-entropy in per-dataset SASRec. Compare baseline, objective-only, residual-only and combined configurations; allow baseline to win.
idea.motivation: The selected idea explicitly targets two user-facing failures: older isolated interactions outweighing recent repeated activity, and broad associations displacing recommendations with a specific current connection. Causal recent pools provide a direct route for current-context evidence, while multiple windows avoid imposing a single five-item horizon. Multi-negative competition targets the model-facing Electronics weakness: 20.2% sampled training reversals and a negative lower-tail margin. None of these observations establishes compatibility, ownership redundancy, or improved held-out ranking.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep separate models and explicit routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, unchanged splits, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the effective SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Use one GPU and save all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Profile costs before launching comparisons; all attempts and diagnostics consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not assume the remaining budget equals its initial allocation.

For each valid position t, pool raw tied item embeddings over causal windows of lengths 1, 5 and 20, excluding padding and dividing by valid counts. Preserve repeated occurrences. Compute three softmax mixture weights from the concatenation of the unchanged SASRec feature and the three pools. Initialize mixture logits to zero. Project the resulting mixture with a bias-free Xavier-initialized matrix, then add it through a scalar sigmoid gate initialized with zero weights and bias −2. Preserve baseline normalization and add no normalization after fusion. Keep optimizer, checkpoint rule and other training settings fixed across the primary comparison.

For CE, sample up to 64 unique uniform negatives per user from the nonpadding catalog outside that user's complete training history. Share these negatives across sequence positions. Preserve identity inside the sampler rather than trying to recover it from anonymous loader tensors; retain the required external tuple. Skip and count users with no eligible negatives. Average uncorrected candidate CE over valid target positions; do not describe it as an unbiased full-catalog softmax estimate. The loss comparison jointly changes negative count and objective; a separately budgeted matched multi-negative BCE control would be needed to isolate those effects.

Predeclare configuration order, checkpoint selection, tie handling and stopping rule before new validation queries. Use only the host's pinned macro validation HR@10 for selection. Report all completed and failed configurations, category scores when available, and GPU cost. Do not infer factorial effects unless all four configurations finish. The supplied historical scores are motivation, not a controlled attribution experiment.

Update the predictor writer to restore identical windows, gates, projections, checkpoints and dataset routes in working/predict.py. Verify scoring parity for candidate batches and full-catalog chunks. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Expose the actual trained module as view.model, fused features through log2feats, and consistent predict_score. Define measured sampled margins, reversal rates, valid-pair counts, mixture weights, gate values and residual/base norm ratios. Treat raw-margin changes cautiously across objectives because score scales may change. Use eval mode without gradients and preserve the model's prior training state. Return metrics and metric_definitions, with unsupported fields explicitly unavailable. The interpreter prompt must include actual measurements, definitions and limitations. Do not convert unmeasured perturbations into findings. Only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions are permitted; reviews, item categories, ratings, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unavailable. Keep the twenty-user full-catalog qualitative assessment separate from benchmark selection.
idea.pseudocode:
freeze_primary_configs_and_original_checkpoint_rule()
check_actual_remaining_shared_budget_and_profile_cost()
for config in budget_feasible_predeclared_configs:
    for dataset in FOUR_REQUIRED_DATASETS:
        initialize_baseline_training(preprocessing_seed=0, training_seed=42)
        for epoch in configured_epochs(default=200):
            for user_aware_batch in sampler:
                sequence, positive, baseline_negative = unchanged_training_positions()
                h = baseline_normalized_sasrec_features(sequence)
                if config.residual:
                    pools = [causal_valid_mean(item_emb(sequence), w) for w in (1, 5, 20)]
                    mixture = softmax(scale_gate(concat(h, *pools)))
                    r = sum(mixture[..., j:j+1] * pools[j] for j in range(3))
                    features = h + sigmoid(residual_gate(concat(h, r))) * projection(r)
                else:
                    features = h
                if config.candidate_ce:
                    negatives = unique_uniform_training_unseen_per_user(max_count=64)
                    loss = mean_valid_candidate_CE(features, positive, negatives)
                else:
                    loss = unchanged_baseline_BCE(features, positive, baseline_negative)
                optimize(loss)
        save_checkpoint_using_frozen_rule()
        run_budgeted_measured_diagnostics_on_actual_model()
    write_matching_predictor_with_all_four_routes()
    obtain_host_pinned_macro_validation_HR10()
select_best_completed_config_including_baseline()
report_attempts_costs_category_results_and_unavailable_measurements()

originality.positive: A controlled combination connects adaptive context scales and candidate discrimination to separate observed failures.
originality.negative: Multi-scale pooling, gating and sampled CE are established techniques; this is an incremental experimental proposal.

future_potential.positive: Controlled improvements could motivate adaptive context selection and subsequent tests of recurring-interest representations.
future_potential.negative: Benefits are unmeasured, and learned scale weights would not by themselves identify intent boundaries or functional usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Three causal pools, small gates and candidate CE require modest architectural changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct user-aware sampling, budget accounting, predictor parity and architecture-aware diagnostics require coordinated implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal attention-based sequential recommendation baseline and item scoring mechanism.
limitations: Does not establish equipment compatibility, complementarity, or satisfaction of an already owned function.

related_work.title: ScaleRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes multi-granularity history patches, local and inter-patch attention, and adaptive signal filtering.
limitations: Does not establish learned intent boundaries or gains for this lightweight adaptation on the matched Amazon benchmark.

related_work.title: Comparison of Recommendation Loss Functions
contributions: Analyzes differences among BCE, categorical cross-entropy and BPR, including distinctions between full-catalog and sampled objectives.
limitations: Does not establish a universally superior sampled loss or validate the proposed combination.

related_work.title: gSASRec: Generalised Binary Cross-Entropy for Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Provides a calibrated multi-negative BCE alternative for a controlled objective comparison.
limitations: Reported evidence does not cover these four matched Amazon categories; exact loss weighting must be preserved.
